# dsh-plugin-computer-user

**Virtual-desktop computer use for DeepSeek Harness.** The agent sees your screen
in the right sideb

ar and its mouse acts on that snapshot — not on your real
cursor. It plays its own game; you keep yo

ouse acts on that snapshot — not on your real
cursor. It plays its own game; you keep your computer.

A fork of jing-hy/computer-user that
adds the half it was missing: a visualization.
## The problem

Upstream `computer-user` gives a text-only model genuine control of a Windows
machine. It works, but
you cannot see any of it:

- `computer_screenshot` writes a PNG to a temp directory **for the model's eyes
only**. You never se

e what it is looking at.
- `computer_click` moves **your actual cursor** and clicks. While the agent

works, the machine is not yours.
- You find out what happened afterwards, from the conversation.

For a long autonomous task that is a bad deal: you cannot tell whether it is
about to click the wron
g thing, and you cannot use your own computer meanwhile.
## What this fork changes

**A live snapshot in the right sidebar.** Every capture the agent makes is
published to a dockable p

anel: the screen, the agent's virtual pointer moving
across it, click ripples, the text it types, th

e keys it presses. You watch the
work in progress.

**Actions land on the snapshot by default.** `link_mode: virtual` means the
agent still screenshots,

still "clicks", still "types" — but that pointer lives
on the panel. Nothing reaches Win32 `SendInp

ut`, so your cursor, your focus, and
your window layout are untouched. The agent plays in the pictur

e; your desktop
is yours.

**Flip to real when you mean it.** One toolbar button (or the settings card)
switches `link_mode` to

`real`, and now the Win32 path runs — with the panel
still mirroring what happens, so `real` mode i
s visible rather than a hijack.

**You can point at things.** Click anywhere on the snapshot, optionally with a
note, and that become

s a queued instruction with an exact screen coordinate. The
agent reads them through `computer_get_v

ision`, so "click *this*" stops being a
description problem.

**The agent gets numbers, not just a picture.** `computer_get_vision` reports the
captured size, the

virtual-screen origin, the capture scale, the current
pointer, the frame's age, and your pending hi

nts. Combined with the panel, the
look-act-verify loop closes on both sides.
## How the two halves fit together
| | upstream | this fork |

| capture | PNG to disk for the model | **same PNG, published to the sidebar** |
| pointer | real cu

rsor via SendInput | **virtual pointer on the snapshot** (default) |
| typing / keys | real keystrok

es | **drawn on the snapshot** (default) |
| verification | screenshot again, read it | **screenshot

again, watch it** |
| user input | none | **click the snapshot to point, with a note** |
| real con
trol | always | **opt-in, one switch** |

Everything upstream did is still here: all nine `computer_*` tools, the four run
modes, `/computer`

approval, the settings namespace, the output guard that
bounces tool calls written as prose, and the

bundled PowerShell that needs no
native module.

Then add the package to your DSH profile as a plugin dependency. The bundle patch
in `cordis.patch.y
ml` inserts the plugin row and sets the defaults:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Settings
Settings → 电脑操作. The two that matter sit at the top:
**动作落点 (link_mode)**

- `virtual` *(default)* — mouse and keyboard only affect the sidebar snapshot.
Your desktop and curs

or are untouched.
- `real` — Win32 `SendInput` drives this machine. The agent takes the real cursor.
**运行模式 (mode)**

- `disabled` — refuse every tool call.
- `readonly` — screenshot, cursor, vision reads, wait.
- `man

ual` *(default)* — acting tools need `/computer` approval in the conversation.
- `auto` — the model
may call everything.

Advanced: capture interval (how often the panel refreshes), screenshot directory,
typing interval, s

croll units, whether the AI may change its own modes, the
output guard, and debug logging.
## The panel
| control | what it does |

| 虚拟快照 / 实机接管 badge | which mode is live, at a glance |
| `→ real` / `→ virtual` | switch `link_mode

` in one click |
| `−` / `＋` / `%` | zoom; `100%` is real 1:1, one panel pixel per snapshot pixel |

| 适应 (Fit) | whole snapshot, centred, **aspect ratio preserved** |
| 1:1 | original pixels, scrolled

if it does not fit |
| 跟随 (Follow) | pan automatically to keep the virtual pointer visible |
| `⟳`
| capture now; otherwise the panel refreshes on the configured interval |

Gestures: **left click** = point for the agent (with the note field, if you typed
one), **Shift+drag
** = pan when zoomed in, **Ctrl/⌘+wheel** = zoom.

The snapshot is never stretched. It is scaled by whichever axis fits and centred
on the other, so th

e shapes you see are the shapes on screen — which is what
makes clicking it meaningful.
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The split that makes the fork work is `ports.ts`: a tool asks a `DesktopPort` to
click, and whether

that means "really click" or "draw a click on the panel" is
one swap. `link_mode` changes which port

is returned; nothing else in the tool
layer knows the difference. It also means the whole tool set

is testable without
touching a real desktop — the tests do exactly that. The Host keeps only the
lat

est 24 generated panel previews and removes its generated screenshots on an
orderly shutdown. A scre

enshot path supplied explicitly by a tool caller is not
managed by this cleanup.

`geometry.ts` is shared verbatim by both halves, which is why a click you make on
the panel and a cl

ick the agent makes through `computer_click` resolve to the
same screen pixel instead of merely clos

agent makes through `computer_click` resolve to the
same screen pixel instead of merely close to it.
## Requirements

Windows. Tested with DSH `0.2.1-alpha.2`; the package also declares the earlier
`0.1.5` and `0.1.7`

lines. Capture uses `System.Windows.Forms`/`System.Drawing` and input uses Win32
`SendInput`, both t

hrough the bundled PowerShell — no native module, no build
step, no external API. On other platforms

the panel loads and reports that
capture and injection are unavailable.
